# Introduction

This vignette computes precursor isolation windows for DIA (SWATH) that each hold about the same number of precursors. The input is a vector of precursor m/z values (MS1 masses), e.g. from a spectral library or a non-redundant BiblioSpec `.blib` file.

`Cdsw$new()` computes the window boundaries (breaks) once, with one of three methods: `"constant"`, `"quantile"` or `"mixture"` (the default). The object cannot be changed afterwards, so we create one object per method and compare them at the end.

# Prerequisites

```{r}
library(prozor)
library(ggplot2)
```

# Constant width method


```{r}
data("masses")
cdsw_const <- Cdsw$new(masses, n_bins = 25, method = "constant")
cdsw_const
cdsw_const$plot()
```


```{r, results='markup'}
knitr::kable(cdsw_const$as_table())
```


```{r}
const_error <- cdsw_const$error()
```

# Classical Method based on `quantile`

Same number of MS1 precursors in each window

```{r}
cdsw_quantile <- Cdsw$new(masses, n_bins = 25, method = "quantile")
cdsw_quantile
```

```{r}
cdsw_quantile$plot()
```

```{r, results='markup'}
knitr::kable(cdsw_quantile$as_table())
```


```{r}
quantile_error <- cdsw_quantile$error()
```

# Adjust windows

Using this method the window start and end is shifted to a mass range with as few MS1 peaks as possible.

```{r fig.width=7, fig.height=4}
optimized <- cdsw_quantile$optimize_windows(min_count = 10)
knitr::kable(optimized)
plot_windows(optimized, masses)
```

# Dynamic Swath Windows with Constraints.

- Maximal window width (`max_window`). Windows should not be too large because of optimal collision energy (personal communication by Bernd R.).
- Minimal window width (`min_window`).
- Number of windows (`n_bins`).
- Window boundaries can then be moved to regions with few precursors (`optimize_windows()`).

`max_window`, `min_window` and `n_bins` are arguments of `Cdsw$new()`. `method = "mixture"` mixes the masses with uniformly spread data and takes the quantile breaks of the mixture, with the smallest share of uniform data for which all windows lie within `min_window` and `max_window`. `plot_breaks()` compares the resulting breaks with the constant and quantile breaks.


```{r}
cdsw_mixed <- Cdsw$new(masses, n_bins = 25, method = "mixture", max_window = 100)
cdsw_mixed
cdsw_mixed$plot_breaks()
```

```{r}
cdsw_mixed$plot()
```

```{r, results='markup'}
knitr::kable(cdsw_mixed$as_table())
```

```{r fig.width=7, fig.height=4}
optimized <- cdsw_mixed$optimize_windows(min_count = 10)
knitr::kable(optimized)
plot_windows(optimized, masses)
```

```{r}
mixed_error <- cdsw_mixed$error()
```


# Benchmarking of the methods.

We compare the optimal number of MS1 peaks per SWATH window (same in each window) with the numbers obtained by using all of the 3 methods implemented.  

```{r fig.width=6, fig.height=3}
errors <- data.frame(
  method = factor(rep(c("constant", "quantile", "mixture"), 2), levels = c("constant", "quantile", "mixture")),
  metric = rep(c("Manhattan distance", "Euclidean distance"), each = 3),
  value = c(
    const_error$manhattan, quantile_error$manhattan, mixed_error$manhattan,
    const_error$euclidean, quantile_error$euclidean, mixed_error$euclidean
  )
)
ggplot(errors, aes(x = method, y = value)) +
  geom_col(fill = "#0072B2") +
  geom_text(aes(label = signif(value, 2)), vjust = -0.3, size = 3) +
  facet_wrap(~metric, scales = "free_y") +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "deviation from equal counts")
```

The error of the `"mixture"` windows lies between the two others: it is smaller than that of the `"constant"` (equal-width) windows, and unlike the `"quantile"` windows the `"mixture"` windows meet the width limits.
